Quick summary (short):

- GPU rec: H100 for lowest-latency SLO headroom; A100 is a good balance for cost/throughput; L4 is viable for cheaper non-streaming inference if you can accept higher 95p latency.
- Reserved throughput estimates (per GPU, baseline model):
  - H100 (80GB): ~120k tokens/sec (~55 reqs/s @350 token outputs with batching), 95p latency headroom ~100–150ms with streaming enabled and KV cache warm.
  - A100 (40GB): ~68k tokens/sec (~30 reqs/s), 95p ~140–220ms depending on batching window.
  - L4 (48GB): ~28k tokens/sec (~12 reqs/s), 95p commonly >250ms for large outputs; best for cost-led, non-real-time workloads.

2) Target scenarios: steady-state 40 reqs/s (business hours), 120 concurrent sessions burst test (10x short bursts), and streaming tail-latency warm/cold.
3) We provision a 2-week pilot reserved pool (1 H100 + 2 A100) with a canary routing policy — route ~10% traffic to the pilot to verify production assumptions.
4) Post-run: we’ll deliver a short playbook with tuning knobs (batch window, KV caching timeouts, quantization profile) and a formal SLO acceptance note.

Alex — a couple of notes on the stress script and what to expect when you run it:
- The runner exercises four modes: cold-start streaming, warmed-KV streaming, high-batch throughput, and synthetic concurrency (many light requests).
- Please use the pilot-metrics-template.csv: we log 50/90/95/99 latencies, tokens/sec, GPU util, and memory headroom per scenario.
- For the model you mentioned we recommend initial quantization to fp16; if cost pressure is high we can test an int8-targeted path (quality check required).

A couple of cautions:
- Streaming latency depends heavily on network egress and app-level buffering; we provide streaming SLO toggles but expect some tail variance in customer infra.
- If you want strict 95p <= 180ms across all peaks, H100 + conservative batching is the only realistic SKU in our experience.

I included a short runbook snippet below (also in the Drive link):
> Run cold-stream test: ./stressplan_runner_v2.sh --mode cold-stream --rps 40 --concurrency 40 --duration 600
> Warm cache (run 10k tokens of warmup across worker nodes)
> Re-run warm-stream test and capture 95p
